blocks.x: Greenhouse climate twin with edge control — energy per kilo down 17% and yield up 6% without a single crop experiment wasted
a CEA operator whose greenhouses were climate-controlled by rules written for a different decade of energy prices. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline quarter priced the rules: energy per kilo of produce 23% above the operator's own best-performing house, climate setpoints identical across houses facing different weather and crops, and every improvement attempt requiring a crop cycle to verify — six weeks per experiment.
The houses' sensors spoke constantly; the climate computer listened to its rules. Between the two sat the growers' judgment, applied house by house, unscaled.

We built the climate twin with edge control: per-house thermal and crop models joining sensor streams, weather and energy prices, control recommendations executed at the edge inside grower-approved envelopes, experiments simulated on the twin instead of grown in the house, and grower overrides logged and learned. The best house's economics became every house's baseline.
